ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is brown with a distinct dark patch covering the tympanum. It features a pointed snout and granular skin with a faint, pale mid-dorsal stripe. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pseudophilautus wynaadensis* is best distinguished by the prominent, dark-brown or blackish patch covering its tympanum, which contrasts sharply against its lighter body.
ai.habitat: *Pseudophilautus wynaadensis* inhabits the evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Dark-eared Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats' understory.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudophilautus wynaadensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches in leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Dark-eared Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 800 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Dark-eared Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from low vegetation within moist evergreen forests.
